claim: Berenson et al. 1995 define snapshot isolation as reads from a start-timestamp snapshot with first-committer-wins on write-write conflicts.
Berenson et al. 1995: ANSI SQL does not exclude dirty write (P0) at any ANSI level other than SERIALIZABLE.
Berenson et al. 1995: lost update (P4) is possible at READ COMMITTED.
Berenson et al. 1995: snapshot isolation prevents lost update (P4) by first-committer-wins.
Berenson et al. 1995: snapshot isolation allows write skew (A5B) that REPEATABLE READ prohibits, and prohibits anomaly A3 that REPEATABLE READ allows.
Berenson et al. 1995: a predicate-read write skew (job-hours example, two inserts) is not precluded by first-committer-wins and can occur under snapshot isolation.
Berenson et al. 1995: Oracle's Read Consistency, stronger than READ COMMITTED, allows non-repeatable reads (P3), general lost updates (P4) and read skew (A5A).

Ports and Grittner 2012: PostgreSQL SERIALIZABLE runs under snapshot isolation, tracks read dependencies with non-blocking SIREAD locks and aborts a transaction in a dangerous structure of two adjacent rw-antidependencies.

Ports and Grittner 2012: PostgreSQL serializable mode has a performance cost of less than 7% relative to snapshot isolation (REPEATABLE READ), headline result on the paper's benchmarks (one machine, 4 to 36 client threads).

Ports and Grittner 2012: on the SIBENCH microbenchmark (one table, single-key updates and full-table scans), tracking read dependencies costs a 10-20% CPU overhead while throughput stays close to snapshot isolation.
Ports and Grittner 2012: DBT-2++ in memory (25 warehouses, 3 GB, 4 threads) SSI causes a 5% slowdown relative to snapshot isolation.
Ports and Grittner 2012: DBT-2++ disk-bound (150 warehouses, 19 GB, 36 threads) SSI performance is indistinguishable from snapshot isolation, with a serialization failure rate under 0.25%.
handles: SSI versus snapshot isolation at scale

claim: Ports and Grittner 2012: on RUBiS (85% read-only, 6 GB) SSI performs comparably to snapshot isolation while two-phase locking suffers lock-contention overhead; the paper's text gives no percentage.
Ports and Grittner 2012: a deferrable read-only transaction waiting for a safe snapshot had median latency 1.98 seconds, 90% within 6 seconds and all within 20 seconds.
Ports and Grittner 2012: on the workloads evaluated in the paper (one machine, 4 to 36 client threads) the serialization failure rate was well under 1%; no high-contention run is reported.

PostgreSQL documentation section 13.2 (version 18), Table 13.1: read committed allows nonrepeatable read, phantom read and serialization anomaly; repeatable read allows only serialization anomaly; serializable allows none.

PostgreSQL documentation section 13.2 (version 18): at repeatable read a concurrent update of the same row raises a could-not-serialize error, and the application should retry the whole transaction from the beginning.
handles: could not serialize access concurrent update

claim: Fekete et al. 2005, read only through a lecture note that restates its Theorem 2.1: in a snapshot-isolation history every serialization-graph cycle contains two consecutive rw-antidependency edges between concurrent transactions.
